config.title: Observability at scale

intro.title: Observability at scale
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple, scalable observability dashboard that visualizes simulated system metrics like CPU usage and request latency. You'll learn the core concept of instrumenting code to collect and aggregate telemetry data, which is essential for monitoring large-scale systems. The main technologies involved include metric collection libraries, time-series databases, and basic visualization tools. By the end, you'll understand how to implement observability patterns that help detect and diagnose issues in production environments.
intro.usecase: In production engineering, observability at scale is the backbone of monitoring large, distributed systems like e-commerce platforms or cloud services. Engineers use centralized dashboards to visualize real-time metrics—such as latency, error rates, and resource utilization—across thousands of servers. This enables rapid detection of anomalies, like a sudden spike in API errors during a flash sale, allowing teams to diagnose and resolve issues before they impact users. Implementing this pattern ensures system reliability and performance at massive scale.

objectives: Implement a centralized logging system to aggregate application events
Configure distributed tracing to monitor request flows across microservices
Construct a metrics collection pipeline for system performance monitoring
Initialize alerting rules based on predefined thresholds and anomaly detection
Integrate observability tools with existing infrastructure components
Manipulate sampling rates to balance observability data volume with system overhead
Render dashboards that visualize key performance indicators and system health

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package to enable component state management for observability at scale.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and hooks
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: React and useState are imported, ready for building observable components.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported React, but remember to also import useState from 'react' to manage component state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. For this lesson, you need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the ObservabilityDashboard component
steps.instruction: Create a functional React component named ObservabilityDashboard that returns a div container.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function with the name ObservabilityDashboard that returns a JSX div element.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the ObservabilityDashboard component here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a functional component named ObservabilityDashboard that returns a div container.
successCriteria: A component named ObservabilityDashboard is defined and returns a JSX div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the component is named exactly 'ObservabilityDashboard' and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've named it 'ObservabilityDashboard' and it returns a div.

steps.title: Initialize service health state
steps.instruction: Inside your ObservabilityDashboard component, use the useState hook to create a state variable called 'serviceHealth' initialized as an empty array.
steps.hint: Call useState with [] as the initial value and destructure the returned array into a variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing state with an empty array
const [items, setItems] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a serviceHealth state variable ready to store service health data.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call that initializes serviceHealth as an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with [] as the initial value and naming the variable 'serviceHealth'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to use useState to create a state variable called 'serviceHealth' initialized as an empty array inside the component.

steps.title: Add metrics section and display data
steps.instruction: Add a metrics section to your ObservabilityDashboard component with a heading and map through the metricsData state to display each metric's key-value pair.

steps.title: Add load data buttons and wire handlers
steps.instruction: Inside the ObservabilityDashboard component's return statement, add two buttons: one with the text 'Load Health Data' that calls the loadHealthData handler when clicked, and another with the text 'Load Metrics Data' that calls the loadMetricsData handler when clicked.
steps.hint: Place the buttons after the existing header and before the service health section. Use the onClick attribute to wire each button to its corresponding handler function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The dashboard will have two interactive buttons that trigger data loading functions when clicked, enabling users to simulate loading observability data.
successCriteria: Two buttons are added with the correct text labels and onClick handlers wired to loadHealthData and loadMetricsData functions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons are missing or not correctly implemented. Make sure to add two buttons with 'Load Health Data' and 'Load Metrics Data' text, each with onClick handlers calling the corresponding functions.
